title: Employment permits in Ireland: all 9 types explained
description: The 9 types of employment permit in Ireland, from Critical Skills and General to Intra-Company Transfer, in plain English.
lede: Most people from outside the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland need an employment permit to work here. There are 9 types.

permits.name: Critical Skills
permits.sub: Highly skilled jobs on the Critical Skills Occupations List. After 2 years you may get Stamp 4.

permits.name: General
permits.sub: Most other jobs, except jobs on the ineligible list.

permits.name: Intra-Company Transfer
permits.sub: Senior managers, key staff and trainees moving from an overseas branch of a company to its Irish branch.

permits.name: Dependant, Partner or Spouse
permits.sub: Eligible family members of some permit holders who want to work.

permits.name: Contract for Services
permits.sub: Your employer outside the EU has a contract to provide services to an Irish company.

permits.name: Reactivation
permits.sub: You lost your permit through no fault of your own, or you were exploited, and want to work legally again.

permits.name: Internship
permits.sub: Full-time students at a college outside Ireland, for work experience in a critical skills area.

permits.name: Sport and Cultural
permits.sub: Work in sport, culture or entertainment.

permits.name: Exchange Agreement
permits.sub: Jobs under international exchange agreements that Ireland has signed.
